$comment: R1762 — THE PREFERENCES SECTION'S PAINTED SURFACES, written down from the
behaviour reference in neutral vocabulary, so the last unjudged section of
the assembled application can be judged against something other than its
own tables.
WHY THIS PIN COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AT R1761. The mechanism to publish a
verdict for a page the host paints landed then (`SectionJudge`), and this
entry stayed open anyway, because a pin that specified only what the build
already drew would be a document that cannot fail — R1747's defect made on
purpose. Measured at R1761 against the reference: this build's preferences
page was MISSING three of the reference's ten rows (a capture-source row
and a retention row in the first group, a payload-format row in the
second), had neither the page heading the reference opens with nor the
build strip it closes with, and its four group headings were loose ink no
specification could address. R1762 built all of it first; this file is
what became writable afterwards.
THE TEN ROWS ARE THE REFERENCE'S TEN. That is the surface worth having:
the reference's page is a list of rows in four groups, and `rows` below is
that list, in that order, read back out of the frame. A row missing, a row
renamed, or a row that moved between groups all read as a difference here.
HOW A PART IS TITLED, AND WHY IT DIFFERS PER SURFACE. Where the reference
fixes the WORDS a reader reads — the page's heading, a group's heading, a
row's title and the sentence under it, a booked row's verb, the appearance
choices, the payload formats — the title here is those words and the judge
reads them back off the frame. Where a part is a VALUE a session changes
(which capture source is in effect, which buffer size) or a control that
draws no words at all (a switch is a track and a knob), the title is this
screen's own name for it and what the pin fixes is the roster and its
order. `crate::judge` says which is which per surface and why.
WHAT IS THE REFERENCE'S AND WHAT IS THIS BUILD'S. Every row, every heading
and every group is the reference's. Three things are not, and all three are
recorded as remainders below rather than written in as if they were: the
two rows whose values are this tool's own vocabulary, and the payload
formats, which the reference names as two third-party serialisations and
this build names for what they are.

owed.why: The last row of ten, and the page scrolls — exactly as the reference's does. Measured at the opening scroll position: the appearance group is painted at y=872 in a region ending at y=900, so the row's own title is on the frame and the sentence under it is 34 pixels lower, which is below the fold. A verdict read from the paint is about the frame, so it reports what the frame has; scrolling to the foot puts the sentence back and this entry is what says that is the reason rather than a row this build draws short. The alternative was an away-condition of `the page can not show all ten rows at once`, refused for R1742's reason: it would swallow a page that had genuinely stopped drawing a row.
